the_uncomfortable_question: what does CLOSING the loop buy? Measured: rule computed OFFLINE from the bells 0.7057 vs ACTUATED in-circuit 0.6953 - closure COSTS 1.04pp. For a SINGLE-SHOT arc the honest answer is that it buys nothing informational: the advantage lives in the two-copy MEASUREMENT and the actuation is classical post-processing rendered in hardware. It demonstrates AUTONOMY, not ADVANTAGE.
where_closure_becomes_load_bearing: when the ACTION CHANGES WHAT IS SENSED NEXT. Only an in-circuit loop can feed round k decision into round k+1 PHYSICS inside one coherence window; offline post-processing can relabel the past but cannot alter the future.

what_won_instead.exp247_redesigned: STATIC T1-aware history-using ML decoder, both logical inputs, held-out shots
what_won_instead.crucial_caveat: it is STATIC - post-processing, NOT a closed loop. The campaign already tried putting adaptivity IN the loop and found it lost to putting it OUTSIDE.

THE_REMAINING_OPEN_QUESTION: can the CERTIFIED static decoder be compiled into REAL-TIME CLASSICAL LOGIC and moved back into the loop? That is exactly the N4 move (decision -> real-time expression). 241c killed NAIVE rules (debounce), not the ML decoder. If its decision function compiles to a boolean/lookup expression, closure becomes load-bearing because the correction would then alter subsequent physics rather than relabel history.
the_margin_is_not_obviously_positive: gain +0.13 balanced accuracy vs fix-machinery cost ~0.08 fidelity by R4 - DIFFERENT METRICS, not subtractable, and that comparison is the first thing any Type-D pre-registration must settle.
verdict: Type D (LEARNING organ) is SCOPED, not designed. Its naive form is refuted, its winning form is not a loop, and the open move is a compilation question with a measured cost on both sides. No flight proposed.
